newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: DAVIS CUP DRAW
In tennis, Patrick Rafter will play the Czech Republic's Martin Damm in tomorrow's opening rubber of the Davis Cup quarter-final in Adelaide.
The draw sees Mark Philippoussis second in action against Jiri Novak.
Mark Woodforde and Todd Woodbridge team up on Saturday for the doubles match against the Czech pair Pavel Vizner and David Rikl, with reverse singles matches set down for Sunday.
CLASS ACTION OVER OYSTERS CONTAMINATION
Newspaper advertisements will be run across Australia in the lead-up to a class action over contaminated oysters from Wallis Lake on the New South Wales mid-north coast.
The advertisement, to be placed in 11 newspapers, has been redrafted during the first mention of the case in the Federal Court in Sydney.
Leading the class action against the Great Lakes Council and 13 oyster farmers and processors is Sydney man, Grant Ryan, who alleges he contracted Hepatitis A after eating contaminated oysters.
Mr Ryan's solicitor, Andrew Grech, says anyone who suspects they've caught the virus from the oysters should respond to the advertisements immediately.
UNION CLAIMS JOBS AT RISK AFTER MERGER
The Finance Sector Union claims as many as 50 branches could close and the jobs of 15-hundred workers are at risk, from the Westpac takeover bid for the Bank of Melbourne.
Union joint national secretary, Tony Beck, says while it's early days, the Union is concerned Westpac may adopt a slash and burn mentality.
The union wants any redundancies to be voluntary.

It also believes today's merger pre-empts the details of next week's Wallis Inquiry into banking, saying it threatens the security of thousands of jobs and career opportunities in the banking industry.
Federal Treasurer, Peter Costello, says he'll judge any bank merger application according to the response the Government gives to the recommendations of the Wallis inquiry.
SOLDIER SERIOUSLY INJURED AFTER EMERGENCY LANDING
A Pentagon spokesman has decribed the emergency landing of a warplane from the U-S aircraft carrier Independence, at Williamtown airbase near Newcastle, as a freak accident.
A joint American Navy-Australian Airforce investigation has begun into the incident, in which a crewman on the Independence was seriously injured.

The Hornet jet reported engine failure while on night manoeuvres off the coast of Newcastle, and sustained damage to its undercarriage while attempting to land on the Independence. The airman suffered serious injuries after being hit by a hatch which was struck by the plane's wing tip.
He's in a serious but stable condition in Sydney's Prince Of Wales Hospital, and will be in surgery for most of the day.
SYDNEY AIRPORT TRIALS AIRCRAFT LIMITS
The Federal Transport Minister says legislation limiting aircraft movements at Sydney airport will be in place by the end of this year.
John Sharp says he's asked airlines to trial a new flight schedule which will relieve congestion during arrivals and departures, and allow a cap of 80 aircraft movements per hour to be maintained.
Mr Sharp says it's necessary to allow some time to test the new schedule - called a slot system - before enshrining the limit on flight movements in legislation.
